newsitem.title: GERMANY: German equities end post-Xmas bourse trade higher.
newsitem.headline: German equities end post-Xmas bourse trade higher.

text.p: Germany's 30-share DAX index ended its first session on Friday after the festive season in positive territory, as those traders not still on holiday took heart from the continued strength of the dollar.

After what was described as very low-volume trade, the DAX index, which gauges trade in 30 of Germany's blue-chip companies, ended up 7.31 points, or 0.26 percent, at 2,852.88 points, as the bull market continued to prevail, despite some consolidation before Christmas.
"One half to two-thirds of people are still on holiday and we are not seeing much volume. Some people are getting ready for the year-end next week," said one Frankfurt trader.
There was little in the way of economic or corporate data to drive the market to any significant gains.

Shares in industrial giant Daimler Benz AG ended 1.05 marks higher at 103.65 marks, after its vehicle-making unit Mercedes Benz said its profit for 1996 would exceed the previous year and it expected record deliveries of trucks and cars in 1997.

One of the strongest gainers on the DAX-30 was diversified utility Viag AG, which ended floor trade up 5.90 marks at 604 marks after a positive reaction to an announcement that it held a 10.24 percent stake in the Munich-based bank Bayerische Vereinsbank AG.
